name: Greifvogelpark Umhausen
kurzbeschreibung: Greifvogelpark Umhausen in the Ötztal: 5,000 m² open-air arena by the Stuibenfall with 30 birds of prey, breathtaking flight shows, and falconry educational trail.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Greifvogelpark Umhausen lies at the foot of the mighty Stuibenfall—Tyrol's tallest waterfall—in the lower Ötztal (Imst district) at an altitude of roughly 1,040 metres. Nestled in a natural larch grove directly adjacent to the renowned Ötzi-Dorf, the facility was designed in strict accordance with animal welfare and heritage preservation standards across a 5,000-square-metre open-air arena. Home to around 30 bird of prey species from across the globe, the park gives visitors of all ages fascinating insights into traditional alpine falconry, an art form recognised by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

Flight Demonstrations & Species Conservation

At the heart of the park is the spacious open-air flight arena seating 300 spectators: during the daily 45-minute flight shows, state-certified falconers present the majestic sovereigns of the skies in free flight against the imposing backdrop of the Ötztaler Alpen. Visitors experience firsthand how snow-white snowy owls glide noiselessly just above spectators' heads, agile peregrine falcons swoop down in lightning-fast dives onto the lure, and mighty imperial eagles, golden eagles, and griffon vultures with wingspans exceeding 2.50 metres harness thermal updrafts. In the process, the falconers provide engaging and educational commentary on hunting techniques, sensory abilities, and the essential ecological role of birds of prey as nature's health keepers. Along an accessible falconry educational trail featuring spacious aviaries, informative display boards and audio stations present native owls, red kites, buzzards, and falcons, as well as international breeding and conservation initiatives dedicated to protecting endangered bird of prey populations.

Visit & Getting There

Greifvogelpark Umhausen is open from early May to late October from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays; open daily in July and August). Flight demonstrations take place at 11:30 and 14:30 (with an additional show at 16:00 on Sundays and public holidays; in cases of torrential rain or high winds, flight shows are cancelled for animal safety). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €12.00, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €6.50, young children free; combined ticket with Ötzi-Dorf adults approx. €19.00, children approx. €10.50. Holders of the Ötztal Inside Summer Card enjoy free admission! Arriving by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Ötztal), continue on the B186 for approximately 15 km to Umhausen, follow signs to parking at Bischoffsplatz/Ötzi-Dorf (paid parking, approx. €5.00 per day). By public transport: ÖBB train to Bahnhof Ötztal, then take bus line 4194 directly to the stop Umhausen Feuerwehr (from there, a ten-minute walk through the Kurpark leads to the entrance).

Tips

The entire Greifvogelpark and the grandstand of the flight arena are completely barrier-free and step-free for wheelchair users; dogs are not permitted inside the park for safety reasons (complimentary shaded dog kennels are provided at the entrance). Combine your visit with an excursion to the neighbouring Ötzi-Dorf and an easy walk to the first observation platform overlooking the Stuibenfall waterfall.
